questions.stem: A patient receives moderate sedation during a regional anesthetic. The anesthesia provider is asked to briefly leave the room while the surgeon continues. Which action is consistent with ASA Standard I?
options: Remain in the room throughout the anesthetic
Leave if continuous physiologic monitoring remains active
Leave after confirming stable vital signs
Leave once the regional block is functioning
questions.explanation: ASA Standard I requires qualified anesthesia personnel to remain in the room throughout general anesthesia, regional anesthesia, and monitored anesthesia care.

questions.stem: An oxygen E-cylinder reads approximately 1,000 psig before transport. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
options: Approximately three quarters of the usable oxygen remains
Approximately half of the usable oxygen remains
Usable oxygen remains full until pressure falls below 745 psig
Cylinder contents cannot be estimated from pressure alone
questions.explanation: Oxygen is stored as compressed gas; the lecture gives about 1,900–2,200 psig when full, so roughly 1,000 psig represents about half of a full cylinder.

questions.stem: ETCO₂ gradually rises during an otherwise unchanged low-flow anesthetic. Inspired CO₂ also begins to increase. Which equipment problem is most consistent with the lecture?
questions.explanation: Exhausted absorbent no longer removes carbon dioxide effectively, allowing rebreathing and a rising inspired/expired CO₂ pattern.

questions.stem: During volume-controlled ventilation, peak inspiratory pressure rises from 20 to 35 cm H₂O while plateau pressure remains 18 cm H₂O. Which change best explains this pattern?
questions.explanation: An isolated increase in peak pressure with little change in plateau pressure indicates increased airway resistance or inspiratory flow.

questions.stem: A nitrous oxide E-cylinder has been used for several minutes but still reads about 745 psig. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
options: The pressure gauge cannot measure nitrous oxide
Liquid nitrous oxide remains in the cylinder
questions.explanation: Nitrous oxide exists as liquid and gas in equilibrium; pressure remains about 745 psig while liquid remains, so pressure does not show remaining content until the liquid is gone.

questions.stem: A soda-lime canister appears partly violet at the end of a case but is lighter the next morning. Which interpretation is safest?
options: The absorbent has regained hydroxide capacity overnight
The color change proves channeling has resolved
The lighter color confirms adequate calcium hydroxide
Color regeneration does not restore absorbent capacity
questions.explanation: Indicator color may fade after use because of regeneration, but the absorbent's chemical capacity is not restored; color alone should not be relied upon.

questions.stem: During bag-mask ventilation, which TWO findings are objective measures of ventilation rather than visual bedside observations? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: The lecture lists waveform exhaled CO₂, peak airway pressure, exhaled tidal volume, and oxygen saturation as objective measures; chest movement and leak are clinical observations.

questions.stem: Peak and plateau airway pressures both rise after pneumoperitoneum, with their difference remaining nearly unchanged. Which mechanism best fits this pattern?
questions.explanation: A rise in both peak and plateau pressures suggests decreased compliance or increased tidal volume; pneumoperitoneum is listed as a cause of decreased compliance.

questions.stem: After attaching a replacement oxygen E-cylinder, gas leaks audibly at the yoke. Which correction best matches the lecture?
options: Verify a single Bodok washer and proper cylinder seating
Open the cylinder fully to force the seal closed
Add a second washer and retighten the retaining screw
Bypass the yoke and increase pipeline oxygen flow
questions.explanation: The lecture directs use of only one washer during cylinder replacement and checking for leaks without overtightening.

questions.stem: Which THREE conditions promote Compound A formation from sevoflurane? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: The lecture states that Compound A production is promoted by warmer, drier absorbent and lower fresh-gas flows, as well as higher sevoflurane concentrations.

questions.stem: A lightly sedated patient needs an airway adjunct but continues to have intact oropharyngeal reflexes. Which choice best matches the lecture?
questions.explanation: NPAs are better tolerated than OPAs in awake patients; an OPA may stimulate oropharyngeal and laryngeal reflexes.

questions.stem: A mechanically ventilated patient develops a partial circuit disconnect. Which THREE monitored values may subtly decrease before alarm thresholds are reached? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: The lecture specifically notes subtle decreases in peak inspiratory pressure, exhaled volume, and ETCO₂ with a small leak or partial disconnect.

questions.stem: An oxygen cylinder enters the anesthesia machine at 2,000 psig. Which component should reduce this high, variable pressure to approximately 45 psig?
questions.explanation: The first-stage pressure regulator reduces high, variable cylinder pressure to about 45 psi before gas enters the intermediate-pressure system.

questions.stem: Absorbent granules are made substantially smaller than the recommended 4–8 mesh. Which tradeoff is most likely?
options: Greater reactive surface with greater gas-flow resistance
Less reactive surface with greater gas-flow resistance
Greater reactive surface with lower gas-flow resistance
Less reactive surface with lower gas-flow resistance
questions.explanation: Smaller particles increase surface area for reaction but also increase resistance to gas flow; 4–8 mesh balances these properties.

questions.stem: Which THREE are recognized approaches to cricothyrotomy in the lecture? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: The lecture lists needle, percutaneous, and surgical cricothyrotomy as approaches to emergency access through the cricothyroid membrane.

questions.stem: An oxygen analyzer displays 50% inspired oxygen while the pulse oximeter falls to 84%. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: The inspired oxygen concentration excludes a respiratory problem
The oxygen analyzer must be reading falsely high
The pulse oximeter must be reading falsely low
Adequate circuit oxygen does not guarantee adequate arterial oxygenation
questions.explanation: The lecture explicitly states that adequate inspired oxygen concentration does not guarantee adequate arterial oxygenation.

questions.stem: A cylinder with pin positions 3 and 5 is brought to the machine. Which gas is it indexed for?
questions.explanation: The lecture gives PISS positions 3 and 5 for nitrous oxide, 2 and 5 for oxygen, and 1 and 5 for air.

questions.stem: A closed-reservoir scavenging interface has inadequate hospital suction. Which finding should occur as reservoir pressure rises?
options: Open atmospheric ports prevent any pressure increase
Negative-pressure relief opens and entrains room air
Reservoir bag collapses from excessive negative pressure
Positive-pressure relief opens and vents waste gas
questions.explanation: With insufficient suction in a closed interface, reservoir pressure rises until the positive-pressure pop-off opens and vents waste gas into the room.

questions.stem: A patient is scheduled for oromaxillofacial surgery and the circuit connector must be directed away from the surgical field. Which tube feature best addresses this need?
questions.explanation: RAE tubes have a preformed bend designed to direct the connector away from the surgical field.

questions.stem: A patient has received a nondepolarizing neuromuscular blocker. Which monitoring approach does the lecture prefer when available?
questions.explanation: The lecture states that neuromuscular response must be monitored when blockers are used and recommends quantitative monitoring when available.

questions.stem: The pipeline oxygen supply is lost, but a full oxygen cylinder is open. At which machine pressure system do the regulated cylinder supply and pipeline supply converge?
questions.explanation: The intermediate-pressure system receives both regulated cylinder gas and pipeline gas.

questions.stem: A closed scavenging interface reservoir bag repeatedly collapses during ventilation. Which system condition is most likely?
questions.explanation: Excessive hospital vacuum creates excessive negative pressure; the negative-pressure relief valve should open and entrain room air.

questions.stem: Which pairing correctly describes direct laryngoscope blade action?
options: Macintosh: direct lift; Miller: direct lift
Macintosh: indirect lift; Miller: indirect lift
Macintosh: direct lift; Miller: indirect lift
Macintosh: indirect lift; Miller: direct lift
questions.explanation: The Macintosh blade indirectly lifts the epiglottis by tensioning the glossoepiglottic ligament; the Miller blade directly lifts the epiglottis.

questions.stem: During an inspiratory pause with no gas flow, which measured pressure most closely reflects static compliance?
questions.explanation: Plateau pressure is measured during an inspiratory pause when flow is absent and mirrors static compliance.

questions.stem: A low-flow anesthetic is planned. Why is the carbon dioxide absorber essential in this setting?
options: Volatile-agent vapor pressure falls as fresh-gas flow decreases
Pipeline pressure falls as fresh-gas flow decreases
Rebreathing increases as fresh-gas flow decreases
Waste-gas suction decreases as fresh-gas flow decreases
questions.explanation: The absorber is necessary during low fresh-gas flow because exhaled gas is rebreathed and carbon dioxide must be removed.

questions.stem: A laser is used in the airway. Which THREE practices or features from the lecture reduce ETT-related fire risk? (Select 3)
options: Fill the cuff with saline or water and dye
Fill the cuff with room air only
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies conventional PVC as flammable, recommends noncombustible tubes, notes that cuffs are not laser resistant and should contain saline/water with dye, and identifies oxygen/nitrous concentration as an ignition factor.

questions.stem: A pressure-volume loop shifts so that a higher airway pressure is required to deliver the same volume. Which change is most consistent?
questions.explanation: The lecture describes decreased compliance as requiring greater pressure for the same delivered volume.

questions.stem: A vaporizer has been tipped while filled. Which consequence is most concerning?
options: The common gas outlet closes and circuit pressure rises
The interlock opens a second vaporizer and output falls
Liquid anesthetic enters the bypass chamber and output rises
Fresh gas bypasses the vaporizing chamber and output falls
questions.explanation: Tipping can allow liquid anesthetic into the bypass chamber, increasing vaporizer output and risking overdose.

questions.stem: Which THREE factors increase carbon monoxide production from desiccated carbon dioxide absorbent? (Select 3)
options: Use of desflurane rather than isoflurane
questions.explanation: CO production increases with higher temperature and agent concentration; among listed agents, desflurane produces more CO than isoflurane. Sevoflurane does not produce CO by this mechanism.

questions.stem: During mask ventilation, downward pressure is applied into the soft tissue beneath the mandible and obstruction worsens. Which technique should replace it?
options: Release the mask seal to reduce resistance
Flex the head toward the chest
questions.explanation: The lecture describes placing three fingers along the bony mandible for a tight seal; upper-airway maneuvers move the mandible/tongue rather than compressing soft tissue.

questions.stem: The overlaid capnograms shown below demonstrate progressively slower expiratory upstrokes. Which respiratory property is most directly affected?
questions.explanation: The monitoring lecture states that a slow Phase II (B–C) rise suggests COPD or acute airway obstruction/bronchoconstriction. The image therefore reflects increased airway resistance rather than a flow-volume loop.

questions.stem: The oxygen flush valve is activated during volatile anesthesia. Which gas path best describes the oxygen delivered by the flush?
options: It passes through the oxygen flowmeter only
It passes through both flowmeters and vaporizers
It passes through the active vaporizer only
questions.explanation: The oxygen flush is part of the intermediate-pressure system and delivers high-flow oxygen downstream, bypassing the flowmeters and vaporizers.

questions.stem: During spontaneous ventilation with a circle system, through which valve do waste anesthetic gases normally leave the breathing circuit?
questions.explanation: The APL valve is the outlet for waste anesthetic gas during spontaneous or manually assisted ventilation.

questions.stem: An edentulous patient is difficult to mask ventilate because of poor facial support. Which adjunct is specifically noted to improve the bag-mask seal?
questions.explanation: The lecture specifically notes that an OPA can improve bag-mask ventilation seal in edentulous patients.

questions.stem: A check valve in a cylinder yoke fails. Which hazard is it normally intended to prevent?
options: Transfilling between cylinders at different pressures
Attachment of the wrong gas cylinder
Delivery of hypoxic gas from crossed pipelines
questions.explanation: The yoke check valve permits unidirectional flow and prevents transfilling between cylinders of different pressures.

questions.stem: A nasopharyngeal airway is inserted in an awake patient. Which complication is identified as most common?
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies epistaxis as the most common complication of NPA placement.

questions.stem: An inspired-oxygen sensor is being positioned to detect hypoxic gas delivery. Where should it be placed?
options: Inspired limb of the breathing system
questions.explanation: The lecture directs placement of the oxygen sensor in the inspired limb to detect hypoxic gas delivery.

questions.stem: The hospital vacuum connected to a closed scavenging interface becomes excessively strong. Which protective response is expected?
options: Positive-pressure relief opens and vents waste gas
Reservoir bag expands until suction normalizes
APL valve closes to isolate the breathing circuit
Negative-pressure relief opens and entrains room air
questions.explanation: Excessive negative pressure opens the negative-pressure or pop-in valve, allowing room air into the reservoir.

questions.stem: A removable galvanic oxygen sensor is checked during machine setup. Which action best matches the lecture?
options: Place it in the expiratory limb and verify a high-O₂ alarm
Replace it after every case regardless of performance
Calibrate it against exhaled carbon dioxide and silence the alarm
Calibrate it against room air and verify the low-O₂ alarm
questions.explanation: Common removable galvanic sensors are calibrated against room air daily and the low-oxygen alarm should be verified during checkout.

questions.stem: A pipeline section must be isolated during an emergency without shutting down the entire hospital gas supply. Which component is intended for this purpose?
questions.explanation: Zone valves divide the hospital medical-gas pipeline into sections so a defined area can be isolated for maintenance or an emergency without shutting down the entire central supply. Line-pressure indicators monitor pressure but do not isolate flow.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 28

questions.stem: A canister is replaced but not seated correctly. What problem should be anticipated first?
questions.explanation: The lecture notes that an improperly seated canister can cause leaks; absorber gaskets and seating are common low-pressure leak sites.

questions.stem: A head-and-neck procedure will sharply flex the breathing circuit near the patient's mouth. Which tube characteristic best resists kinking and compression?
options: Saline-filled cuff in a laser tube
Preformed bend in a RAE tube
Spiral reinforcement in an armored tube
High-volume cuff in a standard tube
questions.explanation: Armored/flexometallic tubes contain spiral wire or nylon reinforcement and resist kinking and compression.

questions.stem: During anesthesia, the pulse oximeter reads 100% while the patient has been apneic on supplemental oxygen. Which limitation explains why this can occur?
options: Pulse oximetry may detect apnea late during supplemental oxygen
Pulse oximetry immediately falls when ventilation stops
Pulse oximetry continuously measures arterial carbon dioxide
Pulse oximetry directly measures alveolar ventilation
questions.explanation: The lecture notes that patients receiving supplemental oxygen may be apneic for several minutes before pulse oximetry detects desaturation.

questions.stem: A vaporizer filler cap is not fully closed after refilling. Which machine test is most likely to detect the resulting problem?
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies a loose filler cap as a vaporizer leak and notes that a low-pressure-system check may detect it.

questions.stem: During mechanical ventilation, the APL valve is out of circuit. Through which route do waste gases leave the breathing circuit?
questions.explanation: When the anesthesia ventilator is in use, the APL valve is out of circuit and waste gases leave through the ventilator pressure-relief valve.

questions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes sniffing position from the triple airway maneuver in the lecture?
options: Sniffing uses occipital elevation plus atlanto-occipital extension
Triple airway maneuver requires occipital elevation only
Sniffing consists only of chin lift and jaw thrust
Triple airway maneuver excludes head extension
questions.explanation: The sniffing position uses elevation of the occiput with extension at the atlanto-occipital joint; the triple maneuver is head extension, chin lift, and jaw thrust.

questions.stem: A NIBP cuff is too small for the patient's arm. Which error should be expected?
options: Accurate systolic pressure with low diastolic only
Accurate mean pressure with high systolic only
questions.explanation: The lecture states that a too-small or loose cuff produces falsely high readings.

questions.stem: Which THREE conditions can increase vaporizer output or anesthetic delivery because of a vaporizer malfunction? (Select 3)
options: Tipping with liquid entering the bypass chamber
Loose filler cap causing a leak
Pumping effect with retrograde pressure changes
Failure to turn the vaporizer on
Overfilling contaminating the bypass chamber or outlet
questions.explanation: The lecture links tipping, overfilling, and the pumping effect with excessive or higher anesthetic delivery; empty/off/leaking vaporizers reduce or interrupt delivery.

questions.stem: During direct laryngoscopy with a Macintosh blade, where should the blade tip be positioned to indirectly elevate the epiglottis?
questions.explanation: The Macintosh blade is placed in the vallecula and indirectly lifts the epiglottis by tensioning the glossoepiglottic ligament.

questions.stem: A rectal temperature remains low during active rewarming while a faster-changing core site is rising. Which limitation explains the discrepancy?
options: Rectal temperature may lag during rewarming
Rectal temperature reflects skin rather than core temperature
Rectal temperature changes before pulmonary-artery temperature
Rectal temperature always exceeds central temperature
questions.explanation: The lecture notes that rectal temperature can lag during active cooling and rewarming.

questions.stem: Which gas-specific connection is described as threaded and noninterchangeable for pipeline hoses?
questions.explanation: The DISS provides gas-specific threaded pipeline connections; PISS is used for small cylinders.

questions.stem: A recirculating OR ventilation system is used. Why can it spread anesthetic contamination to otherwise clean rooms?
options: Recirculating systems have no exhaust pathway
Fresh outdoor air cannot enter a recirculating system
Waste gases become chemically concentrated by the filters
Filtering does not remove anesthetic gases from recirculated air
questions.explanation: The lecture states that filtering does not cleanse air of anesthetic gases, so recirculation can transfer contaminated air to clean ORs.

questions.stem: A cuffed airway tube is used during laser surgery. Why does the lecture recommend filling the cuff with saline or water and dye?
options: The cuff requires liquid to maintain low pressure
The cuff itself is not laser resistant
The liquid prevents all airway fires
The dye reduces oxygen concentration in the airway
questions.explanation: The airway lecture states that laser-resistant tube cuffs are not themselves laser resistant and recommends filling the cuff with saline or water and dye.

questions.stem: A pulse oximeter signal becomes unreliable after severe vasoconstriction and hypothermia. Which limitation is most relevant?
options: Hypothermia increases optical absorption by oxygenated hemoglobin
Vasoconstriction causes falsely high inspired oxygen readings
Pulse oximetry requires high arterial carbon dioxide
Low peripheral perfusion can prevent reliable SpO₂ calculation
questions.explanation: Low perfusion and extreme hypothermia are listed causes of impaired pulse-oximeter operation and accuracy.

questions.stem: A full oxygen E-cylinder contains approximately 660 L at about 2,000 psig. What physical relationship underlies estimating available gas from pressure?
questions.explanation: For a compressed gas such as oxygen, cylinder contents fall approximately in proportion to pressure. The lecture uses Boyle's law, P₁V₁ = P₂V₂, to relate cylinder pressure and available gas volume.

questions.stem: Which THREE practices can reduce operating-room waste-anesthetic-gas contamination from technique errors? (Select 3)
options: Empty the breathing circuit into room air
Avoid spilling liquid volatile agent during filling
Use an undersized uncuffed tracheal tube
Leave nitrous oxide flowing during intubation
Maintain an effective mask or airway-device seal
Turn off fresh-gas flow when the circuit is disconnected
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies flowing gases while disconnected, poor airway-device seals, and volatile-agent spillage as important technique-related contamination sources.

questions.stem: A clear face mask is preferred during ventilation. Which THREE observations does its transparency directly facilitate? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: The lecture states that a clear mask permits visualization of lip color, condensation, secretions, vomitus, and blood.

questions.stem: An arterial pressure and heart rate were last documented six minutes ago during anesthesia. Which standard has been exceeded?
questions.explanation: ASA circulation monitoring requires arterial blood pressure and heart rate to be determined and evaluated at least every five minutes.

questions.stem: A vaporizer is filled with the wrong volatile agent. Which TWO safeguards are intended to reduce this error? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies agent-specific color coding and keyed filling systems as safeguards against wrong-agent vaporizer filling.

questions.stem: Which waste-gas disposal route is classified as active in the lecture?
questions.explanation: Active disposal uses wall suction or a dedicated evacuation system; OR ventilation and through-the-wall routes are passive.

questions.stem: An OPA triggers gagging in a lightly sedated patient. Which property explains the response?
options: It can stimulate oropharyngeal and laryngeal reflexes
It lies in the hypopharynx without stimulating reflexes
It is better tolerated than an NPA in awake patients
It prevents contact with the tongue and soft palate
questions.explanation: The airway lecture states that an oropharyngeal airway can stimulate oropharyngeal and laryngeal reflexes, which explains gagging in a lightly sedated patient with intact airway reflexes.

questions.stem: Which THREE are acceptable ways listed by ASA to continually evaluate circulatory function in addition to ECG, BP, and HR? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: The lecture lists pulse palpation, heart-sound auscultation, intra-arterial tracing, ultrasound peripheral pulse, and pulse plethysmography/oximetry as accepted continuous circulation assessments.

questions.stem: The low-pressure system begins immediately downstream of which component?
questions.explanation: The lecture defines the low-pressure system as downstream of the gas flow-control valves to the common gas outlet.

questions.stem: A scavenging interface is interposed between the breathing circuit and hospital vacuum. What is its primary safety purpose?
options: Prevent carbon dioxide absorbent from becoming exhausted
Prevent excessive positive or negative pressure from reaching the breathing circuit
Increase vacuum enough to empty the patient reservoir bag
Maintain pipeline gas pressure during cylinder failure
questions.explanation: The scavenging interface uses pressure relief to prevent the disposal system from transmitting excessive positive or negative pressure to the breathing circuit.

questions.stem: The cricothyroid membrane is located between which structures?
options: Inferior cricoid cartilage and first tracheal ring
Superior thyroid cartilage and inferior hyoid bone
Inferior thyroid cartilage and superior cricoid cartilage
questions.explanation: The lecture describes the CTM as attached to the inferior border of the thyroid cartilage and superior edge of the cricoid cartilage.

questions.stem: A patient under general anesthesia has no continuous expired CO₂ waveform after tracheal intubation. Which requirement has not been met?
options: Continuous temperature monitoring in every anesthetic
Quantitative confirmation and continual monitoring of expired CO₂
questions.explanation: The lecture requires clinical assessment plus identification of expired CO₂ for ETT/SGA position and continual quantitative ETCO₂ monitoring until removal or transfer.

questions.stem: Which THREE statements correctly describe oxygen, nitrous oxide, and medical air E-cylinders? (Select 3)
options: Oxygen remains at 745 psig while liquid remains
Medical air is stored as compressed gas
Nitrous oxide content is best estimated from pressure while liquid remains
Oxygen is stored as compressed gas at room temperature
Nitrous oxide exists as liquid and gas at room temperature under pressure
Medical air is stored primarily as liquid at room temperature
questions.explanation: The lecture lists oxygen and medical air as gases and nitrous oxide as liquid/gas in E-cylinders; N₂O pressure stays near 745 psig while liquid remains.

questions.stem: Which THREE volatile agents are identified as capable of producing carbon monoxide with desiccated carbon dioxide absorbent? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies the difluoromethyl ethers desflurane, enflurane, and isoflurane as CO-producing agents with desiccated absorbent; sevoflurane and halothane do not.

questions.stem: Which TWO characteristics distinguish an armored tracheal tube from a RAE tube? (Select 2)
options: Armored design is specifically laser resistant
Armored tube is designed only for nasal insertion
RAE tube prevents cuff ignition during laser surgery
RAE design contains a spiral metal shaft
questions.explanation: Armored tubes contain spiral reinforcement to resist kinking/compression; RAE tubes have a preformed bend to direct the connector away from the field.

questions.stem: A pulse-oximeter alarm changes pitch as saturation falls. What advantage is emphasized in the lecture?
options: Continuous measurement of tissue oxygen utilization
Direct measurement of arterial oxygen tension
Earlier detection of carbon dioxide retention
Auditory recognition of subtle oxygenation changes
questions.explanation: Variable-pitch pulse-oximeter alarms are recommended because they allow early recognition of subtle oxygenation changes through hearing.

questions.stem: During a pipeline cross-connection, supply pressure remains normal. Which monitor is the final check of the gas actually reaching the breathing system?
questions.explanation: Pressure-based safety devices cannot identify gas composition; the inspired oxygen analyzer measures oxygen concentration in the breathing system.

questions.stem: Which THREE statements describe an open-reservoir scavenging interface? (Select 3)
options: It isolates pressure using two mechanical relief valves
It uses a spring-loaded pop-in valve
It requires a closed reservoir bag
It avoids positive- and negative-pressure buildup
Its relief ports are open to atmosphere
questions.explanation: The lecture describes the open interface as valveless with atmospheric relief ports that prevent positive- or negative-pressure buildup.

questions.stem: During direct laryngoscopy, which blade is designed to directly capture and lift the epiglottis?
questions.explanation: The Miller is a straight laryngoscope blade designed to pass beneath and directly lift or entrap the epiglottis. The curved Macintosh blade instead sits in the vallecula and elevates the epiglottis indirectly through the glossoepiglottic ligament.

questions.stem: A pressure-volume loop becomes wider horizontally for the same delivered volume after insufflation. Which interpretation is best?
options: The capnogram baseline has increased because rebreathing is present
More pressure is required because compliance has decreased
Less pressure is required because compliance has increased
Expiratory flow has increased because resistance has decreased
questions.explanation: The P-V loop displays pressure versus volume; decreased compliance means more pressure is needed for the same volume. Laparoscopic insufflation is listed as a cause.

questions.stem: A vaporizer is overfilled while turned on. Which complication is described?
options: Reduction of cylinder pressure to approximately 45 psig
Contamination of the bypass chamber or outlet with risk of overdose
Collapse of the scavenger reservoir bag from excessive suction
Failure of the PISS pins with risk of wrong-cylinder attachment
questions.explanation: Overfilling, especially while the vaporizer is on or improperly positioned, can contaminate the bypass chamber/outlet and risk overdose.

questions.stem: Which TWO benefits of carbon dioxide absorption become more pronounced as fresh-gas flow decreases? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: The lecture notes that absorbent use partially conserves exhaled humidity and heat, with both benefits optimized as flow decreases.

questions.stem: Which TWO findings are clinical rather than objective measures used to judge bag-mask ventilation? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: The lecture classifies chest movement and excessive gas leak as clinical measures; the other listed measures are objective.

questions.stem: During an alarm, the waveform appears abnormal but the patient seems stable. Which response best matches the lecture's alarm guidance?
options: Raise the alarm threshold before investigating
Assume artifact until a second monitor also alarms
Evaluate the cause rather than dismissing the alarm
Silence the alarm if the patient appears clinically unchanged
questions.explanation: The lecture states that every alarm must be evaluated and warns against cognitive bias that dismisses valid alarms as artifact.

questions.stem: A flowmeter is operating at low gas flow where flow is predominantly laminar. Which gas property most influences calibration?
questions.explanation: At low laminar flow, viscosity predominates; at higher turbulent flow, density becomes more important.

questions.stem: Which source is emphasized as the major cause of operating-room anesthetic contamination?
questions.explanation: The lecture states that 94%–99% of OR anesthetic contamination is caused by errors in anesthesia technique.

questions.stem: An airway fire occurs during laser surgery. Which THREE factors are specifically identified as affecting ETT ignition risk? (Select 3)
options: Direct contact with the heat source
Use of a preformed RAE bend
Choice of Macintosh versus Miller blade
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies tube material, oxidizer concentration, and direct contact with the heat source as factors related to ETT ignition.

questions.stem: A blood-pressure cuff is positioned on a limb below heart level. Which directional error should be expected?
options: Falsely low systolic with high diastolic pressure
questions.explanation: The lecture states that a limb below heart level produces falsely high readings; above heart level produces falsely low readings.

questions.stem: A bobbin-type flowmeter is being read. At what point should the flow be read?
questions.explanation: The lecture distinguishes float reading conventions; a bobbin is read at its upper edge/top.

questions.stem: A nonrecirculating OR ventilation system is functioning as described in the lecture. Which characteristic should be present?
options: At least 15 air exchanges per hour
No exhaust route to the outside
Complete recirculation of filtered room air
Exactly 3 total air exchanges per hour
questions.explanation: The lecture states that nonrecirculating OR ventilation uses fresh outside air, discards stale air, and recommends at least 15 exchanges per hour.

questions.stem: Which THREE problems can result from OPA placement according to the lecture? (Select 3)
options: Epistaxis as the most common complication
questions.explanation: The lecture lists trauma to lips/tongue, dental damage, and stimulation of oropharyngeal/laryngeal reflexes as OPA complications.

questions.stem: A patient has normal inspired oxygen concentration but suspected carbon monoxide exposure. Why can standard pulse oximetry be misleading?
options: Carboxyhemoglobin can cause a falsely high SpO₂ reading
Carbon monoxide causes conventional pulse oximetry to read exactly 0%
Inspired oxygen concentration directly determines SpO₂ regardless of hemoglobin species
Conventional pulse oximetry directly measures carboxyhemoglobin concentration
questions.explanation: The monitoring lecture states that carboxyhemoglobin can produce falsely high readings on conventional two-wavelength pulse oximetry. Laboratory co-oximetry uses multiple wavelengths to distinguish COHb from other hemoglobin species.

questions.stem: Which THREE actions are recommended when replacing an E-cylinder? (Select 3)
options: Ignore hissing if pressure is adequate
Stack full and empty cylinders together
questions.explanation: The lecture recommends proper transport, one washer, listening/checking for leaks, avoiding overtightening, and checking system pressure.

questions.stem: Why should prolonged high fresh-gas flow be avoided over an unused absorbent canister?
options: It can desiccate absorbent and increase carbon monoxide risk
It increases water content and promotes channeling
It prevents volatile-agent degradation by cooling the canister
It restores hydroxide capacity and masks exhaustion
questions.explanation: Prolonged high gas flow can desiccate absorbent; dry absorbent increases carbon monoxide production with susceptible volatile agents.

questions.stem: A cannot-intubate, cannot-ventilate emergency persists despite noninvasive rescue. Which final airway option is identified in the lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies cricothyrotomy as the final lifesaving option in cannot-intubate, cannot-ventilate algorithms.

questions.stem: Which pressure range best identifies the low-pressure system?
questions.explanation: The lecture defines the low-pressure system as downstream of the flow-control valves to the common gas outlet, at pressures slightly above atmospheric.

questions.stem: Which TWO occupational exposure limits are quoted from NIOSH in the lecture? (Select 2)
options: Nitrous oxide as sole agent: 2 ppm
Nitrous oxide as sole agent: 25 ppm
questions.explanation: The lecture quotes NIOSH recommendations of 2 ppm for halogenated anesthetic agents and 25 ppm TWA for nitrous oxide when used as the sole anesthetic.

questions.stem: Which statement best explains why an NPA may be preferred over an OPA in an awake patient?
options: The NPA is generally better tolerated with intact reflexes
The NPA eliminates the risk of epistaxis
The NPA provides a tracheal seal below the vocal cords
The NPA prevents all stimulation of airway reflexes
questions.explanation: The lecture specifically states that awake patients tolerate NPAs better than OPAs.

questions.stem: A patient is receiving moderate-to-deep sedation without an advanced airway. Which ventilation monitoring is expected according to the lecture?
options: Pulse oximetry alone until desaturation occurs
Continuous clinical observation plus continuous exhaled CO₂
Inspired oxygen analysis without clinical observation
questions.explanation: For moderate-to-deep sedation, the lecture states that ventilation should be evaluated by continual clinical signs and continuous exhaled carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: A vaporizer is exposed to pressure fluctuations from positive-pressure ventilation and oxygen flushing. Which malfunction is being described?
questions.explanation: The pumping effect is retrograde flow related to pressure changes and is associated with positive-pressure ventilation and oxygen flush use.

questions.stem: Which THREE conditions can increase waste-anesthetic-gas leakage into the OR from the patient circuit or airway? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies poor mask/airway-device seals and tubes that do not seal the trachea as sources of anesthetic gas leakage.

questions.stem: Which THREE structures or features are directly associated with Macintosh laryngoscopy in the lecture? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: The Macintosh blade is curved, placed in the vallecula, and indirectly lifts the epiglottis by stretching the glossoepiglottic ligament.

questions.stem: A patient is actively rewarmed after significant hypothermia. Which temperature site is specifically noted as potentially lagging behind faster-changing core sites?
questions.explanation: The lecture states that rectal temperature can lag during active cooling and rewarming.

questions.stem: Which TWO components are specifically part of the low-pressure system? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: The lecture lists flowmeters, vaporizers, check valves if present, and the common gas outlet in the low-pressure system.

questions.stem: Which THREE statements describe waste-gas scavenging in the lecture? (Select 3)
options: Scavenging eliminates all technique-related OR contamination
The Joint Commission requires active WAG scavenging
Proper scavenging reduces trace WAG concentrations substantially
The scavenging system collects WAGs from the breathing circuit
Passive disposal is required by The Joint Commission
questions.explanation: The lecture states that TJC requires active scavenging, properly functioning scavenging reduces trace WAG concentrations by about 90%, and the system collects and disposes WAGs.

questions.stem: A tracheal tube must remain patent despite external compression during head and neck surgery. Which tube is best matched to that requirement?
questions.explanation: Armored tubes contain spiral reinforcement and are resistant to kinking and compression, making them useful in head, neck, and tracheal surgery.

questions.stem: A hospital's backup cylinder manifold switches automatically from its primary bank to its reserve bank. What should this changeover trigger?
options: A drop in wall outlet pressure to about 30 psig
An alarm so facility staff replace the empty bank
Automatic shutoff of nitrous oxide at every outlet
Nothing, because changeover is silent by design
questions.explanation: Manifolds switch banks automatically to keep pipeline pressure steady, so clinicians see no change at the outlet. A master alarm tells facility staff the system is now running on reserve, so the empty bank is replaced before the reserve runs out too.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 30, 32

questions.stem: After oral intubation of an average adult, what tube depth at the teeth is typical?
options: About 15 cm in women and 17 cm in men
About 21 cm in women and 23 cm in men
About 27 cm in women and 29 cm in men
questions.explanation: A depth of about 21 cm at the incisors in women and 23 cm in men places the tip in the mid-trachea, a few centimeters above the carina. Deeper placement risks right mainstem intubation, and shallower placement risks cuff herniation through the cords. Depth is confirmed by auscultation and recorded.

questions.stem: Large cannon a waves appear on a central venous pressure tracing. What do they suggest?
options: Atrial contraction against a closed tricuspid
Atrial fibrillation with absent atrial contraction
Hypovolemia with a collapsing central vein
questions.explanation: Cannon a waves occur when the atrium contracts while the tricuspid valve is closed, as in AV dissociation, junctional rhythm, or complete heart block. Tricuspid regurgitation produces large v waves, and atrial fibrillation abolishes a waves entirely.

questions.stem: Some absorbers have a bypass so the canister can be changed during a case. What happens while the bypass is active?
options: CO2 is rebreathed unless fresh gas is raised
CO2 is vented through the APL valve automatically
The circuit is sealed so no gas can be delivered
Volatile agent is diverted to the scavenger
questions.explanation: With the canister bypassed, nothing removes CO2 from recirculated gas, so rebreathing begins. Raising fresh gas flow above minute ventilation limits rebreathing until the new canister is in place, and capnography confirms when inspired CO2 returns to zero.

questions.stem: A flow-volume loop shows reduced expiratory flow and a steeper expiratory limb. Which process is most consistent?
questions.explanation: The lecture states that increased resistance decreases expiratory flow and steepens the flow-volume loop.

questions.stem: In the standard US five-lead ECG color code, where is the white electrode placed?
questions.explanation: In the AHA color code, white goes on the right arm, black on the left arm, red on the left leg, green on the right leg, and brown on the chest (V lead), often remembered as white on right, smoke over fire. Reversed limb leads change lead II morphology and can mimic pathology.

questions.stem: During checkout, an oxygen cylinder is opened, then closed. Over the next minute its gauge falls steadily. What does this indicate?
options: A leak between the cylinder valve and the machine
Normal cooling of gas inside the cylinder
Oxygen being used by the flowmeters as expected
A faulty gauge, since closed cylinders always read zero
questions.explanation: With the valve closed, the gauge reads gas trapped in the yoke and high-pressure line. A steady fall means that gas is escaping, typically at a missing or damaged washer, a loose yoke, or a leaking connection. The leak should be fixed before relying on the cylinder as backup.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 10, 18

questions.stem: Which TWO effects become more important as fresh gas flow is reduced in a circle system? (Select 2)
options: The absorbent dries out more quickly
More waste gas is vented to the room
Inspired gas departs more from the dialed settings
More heat and humidity are lost from the airway
Volatile agent use per hour increases
The absorbent is consumed more quickly
questions.explanation: At low flows, most inspired gas is rebreathed, so inspired oxygen and agent drift away from the flowmeter and dial settings and must be monitored with gas analysis. More exhaled CO2 passes through the canister, so absorbent is used faster. Drying, waste gas, heat loss, and agent use all decrease.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements about medical gas wall outlets are correct? (Select 2)
options: Each outlet accepts only its own gas-specific connector
All gases share one connector, distinguished by color
Outlets deliver gas at the full cylinder pressure
A valve in the outlet closes when the hose is removed
Outlets use the pin index system to prevent mix-ups
Outlet colors are identical in every country
questions.explanation: Wall outlets use gas-specific DISS or quick-connect fittings, and each contains a check valve that seals the outlet when the hose is disconnected. Pipeline gas arrives at about 50 psig, not cylinder pressure. The pin index system applies to small cylinders, and color codes vary internationally.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 30, 32

questions.stem: Which TWO statements describe breathing-circuit compliance during volume-controlled ventilation on a ventilator without compliance compensation? (Select 2)
options: Delivered tidal volume is less than the set volume
Delivered tidal volume is more than the set volume
The volume lost grows as airway pressure rises
The volume lost disappears at high airway pressure
Compliant tubing reduces apparatus dead space
It matters only during spontaneous breathing
questions.explanation: Corrugated tubing expands and gas compresses with each breath, so part of the set volume stays in the circuit instead of reaching the lungs. The lost volume equals circuit compliance times airway pressure, so it grows when pressures are high and matters most in small patients. Modern ventilators measure and correct for it.

questions.stem: A mechanically ventilated patient suddenly develops a higher peak inspiratory pressure, but plateau pressure is unchanged. Passing a suction catheter through the ETT is difficult. Which cause best fits the combined findings?
options: Kink or obstruction of the tracheal tube
questions.explanation: An isolated rise in peak pressure indicates increased resistance. The lecture specifically notes secretions or ETT kinking and recommends a suction catheter to help distinguish these causes.

questions.stem: An invasive arterial-pressure waveform is overdamped. Which pressure error is most expected?
options: The waveform develops exaggerated ringing and a falsely high systolic pressure
The pulse pressure becomes wider because systolic pressure is overestimated
The systolic peak is blunted and systolic pressure tends to read falsely low
The diastolic pressure falls to zero while systolic pressure remains accurate
questions.explanation: Overdamping blunts the arterial waveform and tends to underestimate systolic blood pressure. Underdamping produces the opposite pattern, with ringing and systolic overestimation.

questions.stem: An arterial line suddenly reads much lower than the noninvasive cuff, but the patient appears unchanged. What should be checked before treating the displayed pressure?
options: Transducer level, tubing, catheter patency, and waveform fidelity
Pulse-oximeter averaging time and probe color
Neuromuscular monitor current and electrode spacing
Capnography sampling rate and inspired oxygen
questions.explanation: The lecture advises verifying leveling, tubing, catheter patency, and waveform fidelity before treating an abrupt invasive-pressure change.

questions.stem: Which situation most strongly supports placement of an invasive arterial catheter according to the lecture?
options: Continuous titration of a vasoactive infusion
Routine short procedure in a stable patient
questions.explanation: Continuous vasoactive titration is a lecture-supported indication for continuous invasive pressure monitoring.

questions.stem: A radial arterial waveform has excessive ringing after a fast flush. Which measurement error is most likely?
options: Diastolic pressure becomes identical to systolic pressure
questions.explanation: Underdamping produces excessive resonance/ringing and tends to overestimate systolic pressure.

questions.stem: A blood-pressure cuff bladder width is only about 25% of the arm circumference. Which direction of error is most likely?
options: Accurate systolic but falsely low diastolic pressure
questions.explanation: The lecture recommends a bladder width of about 40% of arm circumference; a cuff that is too small produces falsely high readings.

questions.stem: Which bladder width best matches the lecture's recommended NIBP cuff sizing?
questions.explanation: The lecture recommends a cuff bladder width of about 40% of upper-arm circumference.

questions.stem: A forearm NIBP cuff is used because the upper arm is inaccessible. Which limitation should be remembered?
options: Forearm measurements can overestimate blood pressure
Forearm measurements always underestimate blood pressure
Forearm measurements directly equal central aortic pressure
questions.explanation: The lecture notes that forearm blood-pressure measurements can overestimate pressure.

questions.stem: Which setup problem is most likely to overdamp or otherwise degrade an arterial-line waveform?
options: Air bubbles in the pressure tubing
Short rigid tubing with minimal connections
questions.explanation: Air bubbles are specifically listed as a cause of degraded arterial-line dynamic fidelity.

questions.stem: An arterial transducer is lowered below the level of the right atrium without rezeroing. What happens to the displayed pressure?
questions.explanation: Hydrostatic pressure increases when the transducer is below the reference level, producing a falsely high reading.

questions.stem: A capnogram develops an elevated inspiratory baseline that no longer returns to zero. Which problem should be checked first?
options: Carbon dioxide rebreathing from an exhausted absorber or faulty valve
Loss of pulmonary blood flow from severe hypotension or embolism
Sampling-line disconnection causing loss of detected exhaled gas
Esophageal intubation causing loss of sustained exhaled carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: A capnogram that fails to return to zero during inspiration indicates inspired carbon dioxide and therefore rebreathing. The lecture lists an exhausted absorber, malfunctioning circuit valve, inadequate fresh gas flow, or calibration error as causes; abrupt loss of pulmonary blood flow or esophageal intubation instead tends to reduce or eliminate the waveform.

questions.stem: A capnogram becomes triangular with a sloping inspiratory decline during controlled ventilation. Which equipment problem is most consistent?
questions.explanation: The lecture describes a triangular/sloping capnogram as a pattern associated with a breathing-circuit or ETT-cuff leak.

questions.stem: Which TWO monitoring findings are specifically useful for detecting a small partial circuit disconnect before alarm thresholds are crossed? (Select 2)
options: Subtle fall in end-tidal carbon dioxide
Subtle fall in exhaled tidal volume
questions.explanation: Small leaks may first produce subtle decreases in exhaled volume, peak pressure, or ETCO₂.

questions.stem: A pressure-volume loop shows less pressure required for the same tidal volume than earlier in the case. Which change is most consistent?
questions.explanation: Greater compliance means the lung expands more easily, so less pressure is required for the same volume.

questions.stem: Which condition is used in the lecture as an example of restrictive rather than obstructive physiology?
questions.explanation: Pulmonary fibrosis is listed as restrictive; asthma, COPD, and bronchospasm are obstructive.

questions.stem: A patient has severe peripheral vascular disease and markedly different arterial pressures in two extremities. Which value does the lecture advise using?
options: The radial value regardless of magnitude
The value from the limb closest to the IV
questions.explanation: The lecture notes that significant extremity differences can occur in severe peripheral vascular disease and advises using the greater value.

questions.stem: Which site remains the most commonly used for adult invasive arterial-pressure monitoring because of accessibility and collateral supply?
questions.explanation: The radial artery is described as the most popular arterial cannulation site because of accessibility and collateral blood supply.

questions.stem: A patient has a weak peripheral pulse and a small radial artery. Which technique is noted to improve cannulation success?
questions.explanation: The lecture states that ultrasound with Doppler improves arterial cannulation when pulses are weak or vessels are small.

questions.stem: Which THREE complications are associated with invasive arterial cannulation? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: The lecture lists hematoma, thrombosis, ischemia, embolism, infection, nerve injury, hemorrhage, and air embolism among complications.

questions.stem: Pulse oximetry is normal, but the patient is profoundly anemic. Which limitation is most relevant?
options: SpO₂ does not measure total oxygen content or tissue oxygen delivery
SpO₂ measures mixed venous oxygen saturation
SpO₂ becomes a direct measure of cardiac output
questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes that pulse oximetry estimates saturation but does not measure tissue oxygen delivery or utilization.

questions.stem: Which factor can interfere with pulse oximetry through the optical signal rather than through reduced peripheral perfusion?
questions.explanation: Nail polish is an optical interference; the other choices primarily reduce peripheral perfusion.

questions.stem: A patient is intentionally cooled for a procedure. Which monitoring decision best follows ASA temperature guidance?
options: Temperature monitoring is optional whenever general anesthesia is used
Temperature monitoring is unnecessary if SpO₂ is continuous
Monitor temperature because a clinically significant change is intended
Monitor temperature only if the patient begins shivering
questions.explanation: ASA Standard II requires temperature monitoring when clinically significant changes are intended, anticipated, or suspected.

questions.stem: Neuromuscular blockade has been given and the train-of-four ratio is needed to quantify recovery. Which modality is preferred when available?
questions.explanation: The lecture recommends quantitative monitoring when available and identifies acceleromyography for train-of-four ratio assessment.

questions.stem: An oxygen E-cylinder contains 660 L when full at about 2,000 psig. The gauge now reads 500 psig. Approximately how much oxygen remains?
questions.explanation: For a compressed-gas oxygen cylinder, remaining volume is proportional to pressure. One quarter of full pressure corresponds to about one quarter of 660 L.

questions.stem: A nitrous oxide cylinder is weighed rather than judged by pressure. Why is weight more useful while liquid remains?
options: Pressure stays near vapor pressure until the liquid is depleted
The pressure gauge measures only oxygen content
Pressure falls linearly with cylinder mass from the start
Nitrous oxide becomes an ideal gas only when full
questions.explanation: Liquid and vapor coexist in a nitrous oxide cylinder; pressure remains near 745 psig while liquid remains, so weight better reflects content.

questions.stem: Which safety system prevents attachment of the wrong small gas cylinder to an anesthesia-machine yoke?
questions.explanation: The Pin Index Safety System uses gas-specific pins and matching cylinder-valve holes.

questions.stem: A full cylinder is opened while another cylinder remains attached to the same manifold at lower pressure. Which component prevents gas from flowing backward into the lower-pressure cylinder?
questions.explanation: The yoke check valve allows unidirectional flow and prevents transfilling between cylinders at different pressures.

questions.stem: Pipeline oxygen normally enters the anesthesia machine at a higher pressure than regulated cylinder oxygen. What is the practical consequence when both are available?
options: Both sources are blocked until the flush valve opens
questions.explanation: The lecture shows pipeline pressure around 50–55 psi versus regulated cylinder pressure around 45 psi, so pipeline gas preferentially supplies the machine.

questions.stem: Which component belongs to the intermediate-pressure system?
questions.explanation: The oxygen flush valve is part of the intermediate-pressure system. It receives oxygen from the pipeline or regulated cylinder supply and sends high-flow oxygen directly toward the common gas outlet, bypassing flowmeters and vaporizers.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 26, 36

questions.stem: Pipeline oxygen pressure falls below the threshold sensed by a pressure-based fail-safe device. What can that device do?
options: Prevent all hypoxic mixtures regardless of gas source
Identify whether the pipeline contains the wrong gas
Reduce or stop flow of other gases based on oxygen pressure
Measure the actual oxygen concentration in the breathing circuit
questions.explanation: The fail-safe responds to oxygen supply pressure, not oxygen concentration; it cannot detect a crossed pipeline containing the wrong gas.

questions.stem: Which monitor detects a crossed oxygen pipeline when pipeline pressure remains normal but the gas is not oxygen?
questions.explanation: Pressure-based safety systems can be fooled by normal pressure. The oxygen analyzer measures the actual oxygen concentration delivered to the breathing system.

questions.stem: An oxygen flush is held open during inspiration. Which TWO characteristics explain why barotrauma and awareness of agent dilution are concerns? (Select 2)
options: Gas first passes through the active vaporizer
Flow is limited to about 1 L/min
Gas is delivered only during expiration
Pressure is reduced to atmospheric before entering the machine
questions.explanation: The lecture gives oxygen-flush flow around 35–75 L/min and notes that it bypasses flowmeters and vaporizers.

questions.stem: A flowmeter tube is cracked downstream of the oxygen flowmeter. Why is this more dangerous than a comparable crack upstream of oxygen?
options: An upstream leak disables the oxygen analyzer
A downstream leak increases cylinder pressure
A downstream leak can remove oxygen from the final gas mixture
An upstream leak always increases nitrous oxide concentration
questions.explanation: Placing oxygen downstream protects against upstream leaks because oxygen is added last; a leak downstream of oxygen can still produce a hypoxic mixture.

questions.stem: At low laminar flow through a variable-area flowmeter, which gas property most influences calibration?
questions.explanation: At low flow, gas movement through the variable-area flowmeter is predominantly laminar, so viscosity is the major physical property affecting calibration. At higher turbulent flow, density becomes more important.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slide 43

questions.stem: A spherical float is used in a flowmeter. Where should the reading be taken?
questions.explanation: The lecture distinguishes float-reading conventions: a ball is read at its center, whereas a bobbin is read at its top.

questions.stem: Why are flowmeter tubes tapered rather than uniform in diameter?
options: The tube must maintain constant resistance at every height
The gas density must increase as the float rises
The annular space increases as the float rises
The float must contact the tube wall at high flow
questions.explanation: In a variable-area flowmeter, the annular area around the float increases as the float rises, permitting greater flow.

questions.stem: A variable-bypass vaporizer cools as liquid anesthetic vaporizes. What does the temperature-compensation mechanism do?
options: Directs more carrier gas through the vaporizing chamber
Directs less carrier gas through the vaporizing chamber
questions.explanation: Vaporization cools the liquid and lowers vapor pressure; the temperature-compensation mechanism increases flow through the vaporizing chamber to maintain output.

questions.stem: Which THREE factors are specifically addressed by modern variable-bypass vaporizer design to stabilize output? (Select 3)
options: Back pressure from ventilation or oxygen flush
questions.explanation: Vaporizer design compensates for temperature and flow effects, while check valves/engineering reduce back-pressure or pumping effects.

questions.stem: A vaporizer is nearly empty but the dial is set to 2%. What is the most appropriate interpretation?
options: The fail-safe valve will substitute another volatile agent
The oxygen flush will refill the vaporizer with agent
The vaporizer will automatically deliver 2% from residual vapor indefinitely
Dial setting does not guarantee delivered concentration if liquid agent is absent
questions.explanation: Vaporizer output depends on liquid anesthetic being present; the lecture includes fill level in machine checks and identifies empty/off vaporizers as causes of inadequate delivery.

questions.stem: Which vaporizer error can produce excessive output by allowing liquid agent into the bypass chamber?
questions.explanation: Tipping can allow liquid anesthetic into the bypass chamber and cause excessive output.

questions.stem: A loose vaporizer filler cap produces a low-pressure-system leak. Why can this be clinically important even if pipeline pressure is normal?
options: The leak is isolated from the common gas outlet
The leak is upstream of the cylinder regulator
The leak occurs before pipeline gas enters the machine
The leak is downstream of the flow-control valves
questions.explanation: The low-pressure system is downstream of the flow-control valves and is the portion most vulnerable to leaks that alter the final gas mixture delivered to the common gas outlet.

questions.stem: Which THREE belong to the low-pressure system? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: The low-pressure system extends from the flow-control valves through the flowmeters and vaporizers to the common gas outlet.

questions.stem: A DISS connector is being evaluated. Which feature makes it gas specific?
questions.explanation: The Diameter Index Safety System uses gas-specific threaded connections for pipeline hoses.

questions.stem: Which TWO actions are appropriate if a newly attached cylinder hisses at the yoke? (Select 2)
options: Verify that only one washer is present
Ignore the leak if gauge pressure is adequate
Close the cylinder and inspect the seal/washer
Open the oxygen flush to seat the cylinder
Add a second washer to improve compression
questions.explanation: The lecture recommends one washer, leak checking, and avoiding overtightening; a hissing connection should be corrected before use.

questions.stem: An auxiliary oxygen flowmeter is used for supplemental oxygen. What maximum flow is approximately described in the lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture describes the auxiliary oxygen flowmeter as providing flows up to approximately 10 L/min.

questions.stem: Which safety device is intended to prevent simultaneous activation of more than one conventional vaporizer?
questions.explanation: The vaporizer interlock is designed so only one vaporizer can be turned on at a time.

questions.stem: Carbon dioxide enters wet soda lime. Which sequence best matches the lecture chemistry?
options: CO₂ dissolves only after all water is consumed
CO₂ reacts directly with calcium carbonate to form oxygen
CO₂ is converted to carbon monoxide before neutralization
CO₂ forms carbonic acid, then hydroxides neutralize it
questions.explanation: Water first allows CO₂ to form carbonic acid; hydroxides then neutralize the acid, ultimately producing carbonate, water, and heat.

questions.stem: Why can an actively functioning soda-lime canister become warm during use?
options: The scavenger returns heated waste gas
Pipeline oxygen enters at elevated temperature
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide absorption by hydrated absorbent is an exothermic chemical reaction, so a functioning canister may become warm during use. The generated heat is therefore expected evidence of active absorption, not heating from the vaporizer or pipeline gas.

questions.stem: What marks chemical exhaustion of soda lime?
options: All calcium carbonate has been converted back to hydroxide
The indicator dye has permanently returned to white
Available hydroxides have been converted to carbonates
The canister temperature has fallen below room temperature
questions.explanation: The lecture defines exhaustion as conversion of available hydroxides to carbonates; indicator color may not reliably track this state.

questions.stem: Which THREE factors can make a canister appear usable even when absorbent capacity is inadequate? (Select 3)
options: Uniform color change throughout the canister
questions.explanation: Color regeneration, light bleaching, and channeling can make visual inspection misleading.

questions.stem: A canister has very fine granules. Which combination is expected?
options: Less CO₂-reactive surface area and greater resistance to flow
Greater CO₂-reactive surface area and greater resistance to flow
Greater CO₂-reactive surface area and lower resistance to flow
Less CO₂-reactive surface area and lower resistance to flow
questions.explanation: Smaller granules increase surface area but also increase resistance; 4–8 mesh balances absorption and flow resistance.

questions.stem: Sevoflurane is used at low fresh-gas flow with warm, dry absorbent. Which degradation product is of greatest concern in the lecture?
questions.explanation: Warm, dry absorbent and low fresh-gas flow promote Compound A formation from sevoflurane.

questions.stem: Which TWO changes would reduce Compound A formation during sevoflurane anesthesia? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: Compound A is promoted by lower flow, warmer/drier absorbent, and higher sevoflurane concentration; reversing those factors reduces formation.

questions.stem: A desiccated absorber is exposed to desflurane. Which toxic product is emphasized?
questions.explanation: Desiccated carbon dioxide absorbent can degrade desflurane and generate carbon monoxide. The lecture emphasizes the order desflurane > enflurane > isoflurane for carbon monoxide production, while sevoflurane is associated instead with Compound A.

questions.stem: Which TWO conditions increase carbon monoxide production from susceptible volatile agents? (Select 2)
options: Use of sevoflurane instead of desflurane
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide production increases with higher absorbent temperature and higher volatile-agent concentration, especially when absorbent is desiccated.

questions.stem: Why does low-flow anesthesia require effective CO₂ absorption?
options: The scavenging interface stops functioning below 2 L/min
The APL valve closes whenever fresh-gas flow is reduced
The oxygen analyzer cannot function at low flow
A greater fraction of exhaled gas is rebreathed
questions.explanation: Lower fresh-gas flow increases rebreathing, so exhaled CO₂ must be removed before gas returns to the patient.

questions.stem: Which TWO physiologic resources are partially conserved by rebreathing after CO₂ absorption? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: Low-flow circle systems conserve exhaled heat and humidity after CO₂ has been removed.

questions.stem: A patient is breathing spontaneously through the circle system. Where should excess breathing-system gas be directed before entering the scavenging system?
questions.explanation: During spontaneous/manual ventilation, waste gas exits the breathing system through the APL valve.

questions.stem: Mechanical ventilation begins and the APL valve is excluded from the circuit. Which valve now routes excess gas toward scavenging?
questions.explanation: During mechanical ventilation, waste gas exits through the ventilator pressure-relief valve rather than the APL valve.

questions.stem: Which THREE are technique-related sources of waste anesthetic gas contamination? (Select 3)
options: Gas flow left on during circuit disconnection
Fresh-gas flow turned off during disconnection
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies poor airway seals, flowing gases during disconnection, and liquid-agent spills as major technique-related contamination sources.

questions.stem: A recirculating OR ventilation system filters room air and returns it to other rooms. What limitation remains?
options: Recirculation eliminates the need for scavenging
Filters remove all anesthetic gases but not oxygen
Filters do not remove anesthetic gases
questions.explanation: The lecture states that standard filtration does not remove anesthetic gases, so contaminated air can be redistributed.

questions.stem: Which characteristic identifies a nonrecirculating OR ventilation system?
options: Waste gas is routed through the vaporizer
Filtered room air is returned to adjacent ORs
Scavenger suction provides all room-air exchange
Fresh outside air enters and stale air is exhausted
questions.explanation: Nonrecirculating ventilation uses fresh outside air and discards stale room air.

questions.stem: A closed scavenging interface develops excessive positive pressure because disposal suction is inadequate. Which safety feature should respond?
questions.explanation: The positive-pressure relief valve vents waste gas if pressure rises in a closed scavenging interface.

questions.stem: Which TWO findings point toward excessive rather than inadequate scavenger suction? (Select 2)
options: APL valve becomes the source of hospital vacuum
questions.explanation: Excessive suction creates negative pressure, collapsing the reservoir and opening the negative-pressure relief valve.

questions.stem: Why does an open-reservoir scavenging interface not require mechanical positive- and negative-pressure relief valves?
options: The APL valve directly controls hospital vacuum
The oxygen flush limits interface pressure
Atmospheric ports prevent pressure from accumulating
questions.explanation: An open interface is valveless and continuously open to atmosphere through relief ports, preventing significant positive or negative pressure buildup.

questions.stem: Which TWO disposal methods are classified as passive rather than active? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: The lecture classifies nonrecirculating ventilation and through-the-wall disposal as passive; wall suction/dedicated evacuation are active.

questions.stem: Which statement best reflects the lecture's NIOSH exposure guidance when nitrous oxide is used alone?
questions.explanation: The lecture quotes a NIOSH recommendation of 25 ppm TWA for nitrous oxide when used as the sole anesthetic.

questions.stem: A halogenated anesthetic is used without nitrous oxide. Which NIOSH limit is quoted in the lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture quotes 2 ppm for halogenated anesthetic agents when used without nitrous oxide.

questions.stem: Mask ventilation is difficult because the tongue is obstructing the pharynx. Which maneuver most directly advances the mandible and tongue anteriorly?
questions.explanation: Jaw thrust is part of the triple airway maneuver and advances the mandible to relieve tongue-related obstruction.

questions.stem: Which head movement is required in addition to occipital elevation to complete the sniffing position?
questions.explanation: The sniffing position combines occipital elevation with atlanto-occipital extension.

questions.stem: During two-handed mask ventilation, where should the fingers used for mandibular support be placed?
questions.explanation: The lecture emphasizes supporting/lifting the bony mandible and avoiding compression of submandibular soft tissue.

questions.stem: Which THREE objective measures can help judge effectiveness of bag-mask ventilation? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: The lecture lists exhaled tidal volume, waveform exhaled CO₂, peak pressure, and SpO₂ as objective measures; chest rise and mask observations are clinical signs.

questions.stem: An edentulous patient has a poor mask seal. Which adjunct can improve the seal by supporting oral structures?
questions.explanation: The lecture specifically notes that an OPA can improve the bag-mask seal in edentulous patients.

questions.stem: Which TWO complications are more characteristic of an OPA than an NPA? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: OPA complications include dental damage and stimulation of oropharyngeal/laryngeal reflexes; epistaxis and nasal trauma are associated with NPAs.

questions.stem: An awake patient needs an airway adjunct. Which insertion preparation best matches the lecture for an NPA?
options: Oil-based lubricant to reduce mucosal friction
Water-based lubricant with local anesthetic as appropriate
questions.explanation: The lecture recommends water-based lubrication and notes that local anesthetic may be used for NPA insertion.

questions.stem: Which complication is most commonly associated with nasopharyngeal airway insertion?
questions.explanation: Epistaxis is the most common complication of nasopharyngeal airway insertion because the device passes through highly vascular nasal mucosa. Gentle insertion with water-based lubricant or local anesthetic helps reduce trauma.

questions.stem: Which standardized endotracheal-tube feature is located near the distal tip in addition to the bevel?
questions.explanation: The airway lecture lists the Murphy eye among standardized endotracheal-tube design features along with the bevel, diameters, distance markings, material, and tube curvature.

questions.stem: Which THREE are standardized ETT design features discussed in the lecture? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: The lecture includes tube diameter, distance markers, bevel, Murphy eye, material, and curvature among standardized ETT features.

questions.stem: A maxillofacial procedure requires the circuit connector to remain away from the surgical field. Which tube is designed for that purpose?
questions.explanation: RAE tubes have a preformed bend that directs the connector away from the surgical field.

questions.stem: Which TWO statements correctly contrast armored and RAE tracheal tubes? (Select 2)
options: Armored tubes are inherently laser proof
Armored tubes are only for nasal use
RAE tubes redirect the connector with a preformed bend
RAE tubes contain spiral wire reinforcement
Armored tubes resist kinking through spiral reinforcement
questions.explanation: Armored tubes use spiral reinforcement to resist kinking; RAE tubes use a preformed bend to move the connector away from the field.

questions.stem: During airway laser surgery, which component of a laser-resistant ETT remains vulnerable to laser injury?
questions.explanation: The lecture states that the cuff is not laser resistant even when a laser-resistant tube is used.

questions.stem: Which TWO measures help reveal or reduce the consequences of laser-related cuff damage? (Select 2)
options: Fill the cuff with saline or water
Use a conventional PVC cuff as a shield
Add dye to the cuff liquid
questions.explanation: Nurse Anesthesia recommends inflating laser-resistant ETT cuffs with saline and dye; the dye allows early recognition of cuff rupture.

questions.stem: A curved Macintosh blade is advanced during direct laryngoscopy. Which structure should receive the blade tip?
questions.explanation: The curved Macintosh blade is advanced until its tip rests in the vallecula. Forward lifting tensions the glossoepiglottic ligament and elevates the epiglottis indirectly rather than trapping it directly.

questions.stem: A straight Miller blade is selected. Which action distinguishes its use from a Macintosh blade?
options: Use a preformed bend to elevate the tongue
Tension the glossoepiglottic ligament from the vallecula
questions.explanation: The Miller blade directly captures and lifts the epiglottis, whereas the Macintosh lifts it indirectly from the vallecula.

questions.stem: Which THREE factors increase the risk of ETT ignition during airway laser surgery? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: The lecture identifies tube material, oxidizer concentration, and direct heat-source contact as major determinants of ignition risk.

questions.stem: Head-and-neck positioning is expected to compress the tracheal tube. Which design feature is most useful?
questions.explanation: Armored/flexometallic tubes use spiral reinforcement to resist kinking and external compression.

questions.stem: A cannot-intubate, cannot-ventilate emergency persists. Which anatomical membrane is used for emergency front-of-neck access?
questions.explanation: Emergency cricothyrotomy enters through the cricothyroid membrane, which lies between the inferior border of the thyroid cartilage and the superior edge of the cricoid cartilage. It is the front-of-neck access emphasized for a persistent cannot-intubate, cannot-ventilate emergency.

questions.stem: Which TWO cartilages border the cricothyroid membrane? (Select 2)
questions.explanation: The cricothyroid membrane lies between the inferior thyroid cartilage and superior cricoid cartilage.

questions.stem: Which THREE cricothyrotomy techniques are named in the lecture? (Select 3)
questions.explanation: The lecture names three approaches to cricothyrotomy: needle, percutaneous, and surgical. Fiberoptic bronchoscopy, supraglottic airway exchange, and retrograde nasal intubation are not listed as cricothyrotomy techniques.

questions.stem: During mask ventilation, the mask is transparent. Which finding can be recognized directly through the mask rather than from a monitor?
questions.explanation: A clear mask allows direct visualization of secretions, vomitus, blood, lip color, and condensation.

questions.stem: At high altitude, a flowmeter calibrated at sea level is set to a high flow. How does actual flow compare with the reading?
options: Lower, because thinner air slows the float
Identical, because the tube is gas-specific
Zero, because the float cannot rise in thin air
Higher, as the thinner gas flows more easily
questions.explanation: At high flows, flow through the annular gap around the float is turbulent and depends on gas density. At altitude the gas is less dense, so more passes for a given float position and the flowmeter under-reads the true flow. At low, laminar flows viscosity dominates and the error is small.
questions.citation: Medical Gas Systems in Anesthesia · Slides 41, 43

questions.stem: Under pressure-control ventilation, bronchospasm develops. Which change is expected?
options: Plateau pressure rises to match the peak
questions.explanation: In pressure control the ventilator holds a set pressure, so airway pressure does not climb. Higher resistance means less flow reaches the lungs during the set inspiratory time, so tidal volume and minute ventilation fall. Exhaled volume and capnography are the key monitors in this mode.

questions.stem: During controlled ventilation, ETCO₂ suddenly falls to nearly zero and the capnogram disappears. Which equipment problem should be checked immediately?
options: Disconnection or disruption of the carbon dioxide sampling line
Chemical exhaustion of the carbon dioxide absorbent
A unidirectional valve causing carbon dioxide rebreathing
Insufficient fresh gas flow causing an elevated inspiratory baseline
questions.explanation: A sudden fall of ETCO₂ to near zero with loss of the waveform requires immediate evaluation for airway or circuit disconnection, sampling-line disruption, severe hypotension, massive pulmonary embolism, cardiac arrest, or tube malposition.
